user_stories.story: As the owner, I run the app against PostgreSQL (DATABASE_URL) with identical API behavior, so nothing in the frontend changes.
As the owner, I copy my existing logs.db data once into Postgres with the same ids, timestamps, photo paths and photo order, leaving logs.db and uploads/ untouched.
As the owner, I run the test suite against a separate database (TEST_DATABASE_URL, name ending in _test) that is wiped between tests, and can never hit my real database.
As the owner, I get a clear message if DATABASE_URL (or TEST_DATABASE_URL) is not set, instead of a silent fallback.
As the owner, README.md and specs.md tell me how to set up, run, test and migrate.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: requirements.txt contains a line for `psycopg[binary]` (version-pinned in the same style as the other lines). `import psycopg` works in .venv. No other new runtime package is added.

The environment variable `DATABASE_URL` is the only source of the connection string for the running app (no default, no .env parsing, no guessed database, no SQLite fallback). `create_app(database_url: str | None = None, uploads_dir: Path | None = None, max_request_bytes: int = MAX_REQUEST_BYTES)` replaces `db_path` with `database_url`. If `database_url` is None, the value is read from os.environ["DATABASE_URL"] at app STARTUP (inside lifespan, before init_db), NOT at create_app() call or module import, so `import main` (which builds the module-level `app`) succeeds with DATABASE_URL unset. If it is missing or blank at startup, startup raises RuntimeError whose message contains the literal text `DATABASE_URL` and an example `postgresql://postgres@localhost:5432/dailylog`. `app.state.database_url` replaces `app.state.db_path` and holds the resolved string.

`connect(database_url: str)` returns `psycopg.connect(database_url, row_factory=psycopg.rows.dict_row)` with autocommit off (psycopg default), so `row["col"]` access keeps working and every function still never commits. The `PRAGMA foreign_keys` line is removed (Postgres always enforces FKs). Each request still opens a connection with `contextlib.closing` and closes it; no pool.

SCHEMA keeps both tables and all columns, with only these changes: `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` becomes `id INTEGER GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY` for logs and photos (BY DEFAULT, not ALWAYS). `created_at`, `updated_at`, `path`, `description` stay TEXT NOT NULL; `position INTEGER NOT NULL`; `photos.log_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` unchanged; `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` kept. `init_db(database_url)` applies SCHEMA with a plain `conn.execute(SCHEMA)` (no executescript) and commits; calling it twice is harmless.

Query text is unchanged except exactly: (a) every `?` placeholder becomes `%s`; (b) in insert_log the first INSERT gets ` RETURNING id` appended and `log_id = cur.fetchone()["id"]` replaces `cur.lastrowid`; (c) the two `conn.executemany(...)` calls (insert_log, update_log) become `conn.cursor()`-based `cur.executemany(...)` with the same SQL and the same parameter lists (psycopg 3 Connection has no executemany); (d) type hints `sqlite3.Connection` become `psycopg.Connection`; module docstring says PostgreSQL. `list_logs`, `get_log`, `delete_log` (rowcount check retained), `update_log` (rowcount check retained) keep their signatures, return shapes, ORDER BY clauses (`created_at DESC, id DESC`; `position, id`) and non-committing behavior. Every other function signature is unchanged.

routes.py changes are limited to renaming the `db_path` parameter/attribute to `database_url` (including `request.app.state.database_url`). Commit/rollback, write-files-then-commit, cleanup-on-failure, and delete-old-files-after-commit logic are byte-for-byte unchanged. main.py imports `DEFAULT_DB_PATH` no longer. models.py keeps `DEFAULT_DB_PATH` (still used as the default SQLite source for the copy script and by the real-path test guard); its comment/docstring, if any, says it is the legacy SQLite file.

With the app on the test database, every pre-existing API behavior (status codes, error messages, JSON shapes, ordering, timestamp strings such as `...+00:00` with microseconds, photo order, 404/413/422/500 precedence) is unchanged. All 132 pre-existing tests, adapted as in criteria 13-15, pass. Total passing count is 132 plus the new tests; 0 failures, 0 errors.

New file `backend/migrate_sqlite.py` (single new non-test source file). CLI: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe backend/migrate_sqlite.py [--sqlite PATH]`. `--sqlite` defaults to models.DEFAULT_DB_PATH (project-root logs.db). Target is read from DATABASE_URL only; if unset/blank it prints a message naming `DATABASE_URL` to stderr and exits with code 2. It exposes `migrate(sqlite_path: Path, database_url: str) -> dict` returning `{"logs": n, "photos": m}` and raising `MigrationError` (defined in the script) on refusal; `main()` catches MigrationError, prints the message to stderr, and exits with code 1. Success exits 0.

migrate(): (1) raises MigrationError if the source file does not exist (and does NOT create it); (2) opens the source strictly read-only (`sqlite3.connect(?mode=ro, uri=True)`) so no file is created/modified; (3) calls database.init_db on the target so tables exist; (4) in ONE target transaction: raises MigrationError (and writes nothing) if target `logs` OR `photos` has any row; inserts every logs row with its original `id`, `description`, `created_at`, `updated_at` strings verbatim; inserts every photos row with original `id`, `log_id`, `path`, `position` verbatim; (5) resets both identity sequences so the next generated id is max(id)+1 (or 1 for an empty table), e.g. via `setval(pg_get_serial_sequence(...), COALESCE(MAX(id),0)+1, false)`; (6) commits only after everything succeeded, rolls back on any error (target left empty); (7) prints `copied N logs, M photos` (counts) on success. It never writes to, renames or deletes the SQLite file or anything under uploads/ and never reads uploads/.

tests/conftest.py reads `TEST_DATABASE_URL`. If unset or blank, the pytest run errors (pytest.UsageError or equivalent at session start) with a message containing `TEST_DATABASE_URL` and the example `postgresql://postgres@localhost:5432/dailylog_test`. It also errors, before any connection is opened, if TEST_DATABASE_URL equals DATABASE_URL (when that is set; compare after stripping), or if the database name parsed from the URL path (query string ignored) does not end in `_test`. Tests never read DATABASE_URL for connecting.

An autouse function-scoped fixture first runs database.init_db(TEST_DATABASE_URL) (so the first run on an empty test DB works) and then `TRUNCATE logs, photos RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE`, so every test (including those that build their own create_app) starts with empty tables and ids starting at 1. Each test uses a tmp_path uploads dir. The `env` fixture keeps its shape `(client, db, uploads)` where `db` is now the TEST_DATABASE_URL string, and calls `create_app(database_url=, uploads_dir=uploads)`. The existing session-scope real-path guard (real logs.db and uploads/ size/mtime unchanged) is kept and still passes; `test_real_paths_untouched` is kept.

conftest.py no longer imports sqlite3. `rows(db)` reads `SELECT * FROM logs ORDER BY id` and `SELECT * FROM photos ORDER BY id` through psycopg (dict rows) and returns `(logs, photos)`; `assert_nothing_stored`, `snapshot` keep their signatures and semantics. A new helper `execute_sql(db, sql, params=())` opens a short psycopg connection, executes, commits, closes; it replaces all inline `sqlite3.connect(db)` usage in tests. No test file imports sqlite3 except the new copy-script test (which builds a temp SQLite source).

With `?` -> `%s` and the connection via execute_sql, same intent and same assertions: test_database.py::test_list_tie_break_higher_id_first, ::test_list_orders_by_timestamp_not_id, ::test_list_photos_order_by_position (UPDATE photos SET id = id + 100 still valid because identity is BY DEFAULT); test_logs.py::test_delete_log_without_photos_and_twice (DELETE FROM photos), ::test_delete_never_removes_outside_uploads (UPDATE photos SET path); test_validation.py::test_exact_5mib_ok_and_one_more_413 (DELETE FROM photos then logs). Each of these is recorded in the implementer's report.

Every `sqlite3.OperationalError(...)` raised by monkeypatched database functions becomes `psycopg.OperationalError(...)` with the same message: test_database.py::test_db_error_cleans_up_500, ::test_db_failure_rolls_back_row, ::test_put_db_error_500_cleans_up_new_files_keeps_old, ::test_delete_db_error_500_nothing_deleted. They still prove: status 500, rolled-back rows (the real function runs on the connection then raises, and a fresh connection sees no change), new files removed, old files kept. Monkeypatches of builtins.open / os.remove (test_photos.py, test_logs.py) are not database-related and stay unchanged.

All `create_app(db_path=tmp_path / "t.db", ...)` / `create_app(db_path=db, ...)` calls in test_api.py (restart test), test_photos.py (2 places), test_validation.py (2 places incl. max_request_bytes variants) become `create_app(database_url=, ...)` using a shared fixture/constant from conftest (e.g. fixture `test_url`). test_log_and_photo_survive_app_restart still shows data persisting across two app instances on the same test DB.

New tests (in test_database.py, or a new file only if needed; T012 layout otherwise kept): (a) with DATABASE_URL removed via monkeypatch.delenv, `import main` side effects aside, `with TestClient(create_app(uploads_dir=tmp)):` raises RuntimeError whose message contains `DATABASE_URL`; (b) `create_app()` itself, with DATABASE_URL unset, does not raise; (c) the copy script CLI (subprocess, env with DATABASE_URL removed) exits with code 2 and its stderr contains `DATABASE_URL`; (d) conftest safety logic: a pure function (e.g. `check_test_url(test_url, database_url)` in conftest) raises for equal URLs, for a database name not ending in `_test` (e.g. `.../dailylog`), and accepts `.../dailylog_test`; tested directly without connecting.

New test file `tests/test_migrate.py`. Builds a temp SQLite file in tmp_path (sqlite3, the old schema) with at least: logs ids 4 and 6 (gap, matching the real data shape), descriptions with non-ASCII text, timestamps in the `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffff+00:00` format where created_at order differs from id order, log 4 with 3 photos whose rows are inserted so photo ids and positions are not in path order, log 6 with 1 photo, plus one log with no photos. Using the test database: (a) `migrate(src, TEST_DATABASE_URL)` returns the right counts; every logs and photos row read back equals the source row exactly (ids, description, both timestamps, log_id, path, position); `GET /api/logs` through create_app(database_url=test url) returns the logs in the expected order with photos in position order. (b) After migrate, creating a log through the API gets id = max(source logs id)+1 and the first photo created gets id = max(source photo id)+1 (identity sequence continues past the copied ids, no duplicate-key error). (c) Running migrate a second time raises MigrationError, and logs/photos contents are unchanged (non-empty target refused); also refused when only `photos` is non-empty. (d) The source file's bytes (sha256) and mtime_ns are identical before and after migrate (also after a refused run). (e) A missing source path raises MigrationError and does not create the file. (f) One subprocess run of the CLI (`sys.executable backend/migrate_sqlite.py --sqlite ` with DATABASE_URL set to the TEST_DATABASE_URL in its env) exits 0 and stdout mentions the counts. (g) If a photo row fails to insert (e.g. a source photo referencing a nonexistent log_id), migrate raises and the target logs table is still empty (single transaction). The tests never use the real logs.db and never touch uploads/.

During implementation/verification: no connection is made to database `dailylog` (only databases whose name ends in `_test`); real logs.db and uploads/ have unchanged size and mtime_ns before/after; no process listens on or is started on port 8000; any live server run uses a port other than 8000 and a `_test` database, and the process is stopped afterward. The copy script is not run against the real database. The Python source contains no `AUTOINCREMENT`, `lastrowid`, `executescript`, `PRAGMA`, or `sqlite3` references outside migrate_sqlite.py (and tests/test_migrate.py plus the CLI/other tests in 16-17).

README.md: database mentions (lines currently saying SQLite / logs.db created at runtime / test_database.py description / database.py description / folder tree) now say PostgreSQL and `logs.db` is described only as the legacy file the migration reads. A setup section covers, in order: create the databases `dailylog` and `dailylog_test`; put the password in the libpq password file `%APPDATA%\postgresql\pgpass.conf` (format `localhost:5432:*:postgres:`), so URLs carry no password; set `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres@localhost:5432/dailylog` before starting the app; set `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres@localhost:5432/dailylog_test` before running pytest (wiped each test; must end in `_test`); the exact one-time migration command from criterion 8 and a note that it refuses a non-empty target and leaves logs.db and uploads/ untouched. The run and test commands show the env var usage. specs.md table row "Database" reads PostgreSQL (descriptions, timestamps, photo paths) and any stack/setup mention is updated consistently. No wording that references X/Twitter inspiration is added.
No Docker/compose file, no connection pool, no change to timestamp column types (still TEXT), no new endpoints or frontend changes. .gitignore unchanged.

assumptions.assumption: Env var names are exactly DATABASE_URL and TEST_DATABASE_URL; URLs carry no password (libpq password file supplies it).

The DATABASE_URL lookup happens at startup (lifespan) so that `import main`, which builds the module-level `app = create_app()`, and the test suite do not need DATABASE_URL set. uvicorn main:app with DATABASE_URL unset therefore fails at startup with the clear message.
models.DEFAULT_DB_PATH is kept (legacy SQLite path) for the copy script default and the real-path guard; its name is not changed to keep the diff minimal.
Copy script also refuses when the target photos table is non-empty (stricter than the stated logs rule, same intent). It creates missing target tables via init_db before checking.
The test DB (dailylog_test) already exists and is reachable via pgpass; tests create the tables themselves.
Tests run serially (no pytest-xdist), since all share one test database and TRUNCATE.
Timestamps remain TEXT, so ordering is lexicographic exactly as before; no timezone conversion occurs.
Plain-text TRUNCATE needs no extra privileges beyond table ownership, which the postgres superuser has.

edge_cases.case: DATABASE_URL set but blank or whitespace: treated as unset.

TEST_DATABASE_URL with a query string (`...dailylog_test?connect_timeout=5`): name check uses the path component only; TEST_DATABASE_URL equal to DATABASE_URL differing only by whitespace is still refused.
Source SQLite has ids with gaps (4, 6) and zero photos for a log; empty SQLite tables (copy 0 rows, sequences start at 1).
Photo ids not in position order: list order still by position then id.
Failure midway through the copy leaves the target empty (single transaction, rollback).
psycopg returns identity values as int; JSON output ids stay ints.
A failed request must roll back and close the connection (no leaked open transaction holding locks that would block the next test's TRUNCATE).
The app's startup init_db on a database that already has the tables is a no-op.

risks.risk: TRUNCATE between tests can block if a prior test leaked an open connection/transaction; connections must always be closed (closing()) including on failure paths.
test_logs/test_validation tests that previously relied on a fresh file per test now rely on truncation; any test that assumed ids starting at 1 depends on RESTART IDENTITY.

Windows subprocess test of the CLI needs sys.path/cwd handling because the script imports database and models as top-level modules; the script must work when invoked as `python backend/migrate_sqlite.py` from the project root.
Module-level `app = create_app()` stays harmless only because the env lookup is deferred to startup.
Session real-path guard still reads models.DEFAULT_DB_PATH metadata only; it must not open the file.

dependencies.dependency: Local PostgreSQL 18 on localhost:5432 with databases dailylog (user's, not touched by tests) and dailylog_test; credentials via pgpass.conf.

Files: backend/database.py, routes.py, main.py, models.py, migrate_sqlite.py (new), tests/conftest.py, test_api.py, test_database.py, test_logs.py, test_photos.py, test_validation.py, test_migrate.py (new), README.md, specs.md, requirements.txt.

spec.self_critique: Every story maps to criteria: run on Postgres (2-7), copy (8-9, 17), test isolation and safety (10-12, 18), fail-fast (2, 16), docs (19). Each criterion is mechanically checkable (grep for removed tokens, run pytest with TEST_DATABASE_URL, inspect rows). The new-test count is left open on purpose; the requirement is the listed behaviors, not a number. Biggest remaining risk: the deferred DATABASE_URL lookup is my interpretation of "when the app starts" that keeps imports and tests working; if the user wanted failure at import time it would break the module-level app in tests. No genuinely blocking ambiguity remains, so no clarifications are requested.
